questions.feedback: If you picked 'It disappeared for good', that is the evaporation trap: water disappears for good once it evaporates is wrong - the water is still there as invisible vapour and will return as rain. Reteach point: evaporation changes the form, it never removes the water.
questions.misconception: Water disappears for good once it evaporates.
questions.prompt: A puddle dries up on a sunny day. Where did the water go?

questions.feedback: Condensation is the cooling stage: vapour back into liquid drops. If you named evaporation, you have the two change-of-state stages swapped - the cooling half of the loop needs reteaching.
questions.prompt: Name the stage where water vapour cools into tiny drops and forms a cloud.

choices.text: Collection - water gathers in rivers and the sea
Evaporation - the sun lifts the water
The cycle ends - the water is finished

questions.feedback: After rain falls, the water gathers again in collection, ready to evaporate once more. Picking 'the cycle ends' shows the loop idea has not landed: the water cycle never ends, it goes round and round.
questions.prompt: Which stage comes straight after precipitation in the cycle?

questions.answer: Rain is the evaporated water itself, cooled from vapour into clouds and fallen back down, so it was never gone.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names vapour and the return journey: up as vapour, back as rain. An answer that cannot say where rain comes from means the evaporation-disappears misconception is still live and evaporation needs reteaching first next lesson.
questions.misconception: Water disappears for good once it evaporates.
questions.prompt: In one sentence: why is rain proof that evaporated water is not gone for good?
